Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".

## The gap ledger

The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).

A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.

- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.

Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.

A row states its gap as it stands now. A note adds a fact. If your work changes what a row says, write the row's whole new line with `rewrite` (below), not a note that tells the repair.

The heading reader of `ledger.py` does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.

## Reading the record

Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:
- POSITIONS holds each of the curator's decisions, in one place. Everything else points there. Write a decision there only if your brief gives it to you to record. If you have evidence against one, do as `exploring.md` says.
- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a note directly in `explorations/` or `explorations/reviews/`, add its line to INDEX: ``- `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.

Write the gap ledger only with `ledger.py`, which checks each line that it writes against the row template.

    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"

To add a row:

1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.

To change a row:

- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N. It refuses a note that takes the row past 1,200 characters, or its notes cell past 700 characters. `$L note N TEXT --check` writes nothing. It says whether TEXT fits, and how many characters the notes and the row have left now and would have left with TEXT. These counts include the separator that the tool adds. It exits 0 if TEXT fits, and 1 if not. Run it before a long note, or before a note on a row near its limits. If TEXT does not fit, shorten it, or cut the notes with `rewrite` (below).
- `$L rewrite N FILE` replaces row N with the whole line in FILE, a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with N or `?` in its number cell. Use it to correct the claim, cut the notes or change the reproducer. The tool checks the line against the template and keeps the old line in the history file.
- `$L duplicate N --of M` makes row N a pointer to row M.
- `$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME` marks row N `FIXED`, by the commit HASH and its test NAME. Run it once that commit is in `HEAD`, and commit the close after it. NAME can also be a file under `explorations/coordinator/tools/`, or `none` with `--note REASON`. For a `CONTESTED` row, add `--settled TEXT`, which names what settled its question.
- `$L landing-check BASE` prints each problem, and exits 1 on any. Run it when your brief asks for it. It checks the whole ledger against the template, so a broken row that BASE already had counts too. The problems are a row that breaks the template, an `XXX` test deleted or renamed while a row that is not closed names it, a row that is not closed though a commit says it fixed it, and a FACTS or POSITIONS entry that disagrees with a row's status.

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

# The distance's two crash rows on climb batch 27's merged tree: a probe

Probe of the two `#crash` rows in `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/distance.txt`. I worked in a worktree of my own, `/home/user/fortress-distcrash`, detached at `a2f0b5cf2` and seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base27` (`551b02858`). I built it there (`ant compileAll`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 35 s) and removed it at the end. I made no branch. Nothing in `/home/user/fortress` changed: `main` is still `209192b67`, and `git status` is clean. I committed nothing and filed nothing. The evidence excerpts are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/distance-crash/evidence/`.

## Answer

- **Cause.** The compiled checker's overload resolution sorts the candidates of a call with `candidates.sortWith(moreSpecific)` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:761`). `moreSpecific` is a strict partial order: two candidates can each be no more specific than the other. Java's TimSort, which Scala's `sortWith` reaches through `Arrays.sort`, requires a consistent total preorder. It checks for that only on 32 or more elements; below 32 it uses binary insertion and never checks.
- **The input in `Char`.** The call is `x = -1` in `digit(self)` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:692:13-18`, with `x: ZZ32` and the numeral `-1`). It has 33 applicable `=` candidates. 24 of them are rung N's `=` pairs (`a97d60dc6`).
- **Which rung.** Not rung C: with C's binding put back to the glue class on the merged tree, the crash is the same, with the same candidate order. N brings the input. Whether TimSort throws on the 33 depends on their order. That order is the hash order of the overloadings' names, and each name holds its declaration's line. So the trip comes from the merged tree's line positions, which F, N, E, I, A and W all moved. One blank line inserted at `FortressBuiltin.fss:14` makes the crash disappear.
- **Deterministic.** The gate's run and my four runs of the unchanged merged tree all crash at the same call. The two runs that dumped the candidate order give the same order. The crash does not vary from run to run. It does vary from edit to edit: any edit that moves one of the 76 `=` declarations visible at this call can make it appear or disappear, at this call or at any of the 64 other sorts of 32 or more candidates.
- **What it hides.** The checker skips 30 of `Char`'s 44 members, from the throw to the end of the declaration, including 29 of its 41 helper bindings, and the stage keeps `Char` unchecked. Two one-line local changes each avoid the crash, and each gives `#total 0` and `#crash none`, with `Char` checked whole and 0 errors: the blank line, and a rank sort in the checker. So the crash hides **0 errors** today.
- **Fix.** It is small in code: one line at `:761`, and siblings at `:728`, `CoercionOracle.scala:255` and `Formula.scala:609`. But it is a change to the checker. It needs P-148's time measurement, because my naive rank sort doubled the stage's time, and a test that does not depend on hash order.

## 1. The crash's cause

### Where the gate wrote its log, and what it holds

The workflow sets `LOG_DIR = 'tmp/gate-batch-' + BATCH` and `GATE_OUT = LOG_DIR + '/out'` (`explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:1112-1113`). Step 2 starts the stage with scratch directory `LOG_DIR/distance` (`:1860`). So the checker's output is `/home/user/fortress/tmp/gate-batch-27/distance/run.txt`. I only read it there. Its lines 762-768 hold `@@TC DECL-CRASH ObjectDecl …FortressBuiltin.fss:661:1-773:2 java.lang.IllegalArgumentException … Comparison method violates its general contract!` and six frames, from `TimSort.mergeLo(TimSort.java:781)` down to `scala.collection.SeqOps.sorted(Seq.scala:728)`. The stage keeps six frames because `tools/distance/shadow-patch.py:142` prints `Math.min(6, __st.length)` of them.

### The full stack (my run 2, with that limit raised to 400 in my worktree, which changes only the printing)

`TimSort` → `SeqOps.sortWith` → **`Functionals.typedApplicationOfChecked(Functionals.scala:761)`** → `typedApplication(:660)` → `checkExprFunctionals(:1298)`, the `SOpExpr` case → `Misc.generatorClauseGetBindings(:73)` / `handleIfClause(:127)`, the if-clause's condition → `Misc.checkExprMisc(:528)`, the `SIf` case → `:435`, a block → `Decls.checkLetBody(:58)` / `checkExprDecls(:408)`, a local `x:ZZ32 = …` → `:435` → `:509`, the `SDo` case → `Decls.checkDecls(:221)`, a method body → `Decls.checkDecls(:165-168)`, the object's members in order → `STypeChecker.typeCheck(:432)` → the shadow's `StaticChecker.checkCompilationUnit` → `DistanceMulti.main(:68)`. The frames are in `evidence/run2-deep-stack.txt`.

This is the shape do → let → if → operator, and only `digit(self)` has it: `do x:ZZ32 = myJavaDigit(self,10); if (x = -1) then … end end` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:690-693` on the merged tree). An instrumented copy of `Functionals.scala` confirmed the call (below): `@@SORTX n=33 op=Some(=) args@ FortressBuiltin.fss:692:13 ; FortressBuiltin.fss:692:18`.

### The comparator

`moreSpecific(a, b)` is `moreSpecificCandidate` (`scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1124-1164`). It reaches `CoercionOracle.moreSpecific`, which is `noLessSpecific && !equivalent` (`CoercionOracle.scala:74-91`). `sortWith(lt)` is `sorted(Ordering.fromLessThan(lt))`, which answers 0 when neither candidate is more specific than the other.

For the 33 candidates, my instrumented copy computed the whole 33×33 relation (`evidence/inst1-relation.txt`). It holds 231 pairs. It is irreflexive, it has no pair related both ways, and it has no intransitive triple. So it is a strict partial order. But incomparability is not transitive: **3,880 triples** have i ~ j and j ~ k, but i ≺ k. One example:

- `((ZZ & {BigNum}), ZZ64)` ≺ `((ZZ & {BigNum}), ZZ)`;
- `(QQ, NN32)` is incomparable with both.

TimSort's contract (the result of `compare(x, z)` follows from `compare(x, y) == 0`) breaks there, and TimSort found the break during a galloping merge, at `mergeLo:781`.

There are three sibling sorts by a partial order: `Functionals.scala:728` (`cs.sortWith(moreSpecific).head`), `CoercionOracle.scala:255`, and `Formula.scala:609`. The last is worse: `sortWith((a,b) => isTrue(ta.subtype(b,a)))` is reflexive, so `compare(a, a)` is -1.

### The input in `Char`'s declaration

There are 76 pre-candidates for `=` at `:692`: 57 from `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` and 19 from `FortressBuiltin.fss` (`evidence/inst3-precandidates.txt`). Of these, 33 apply:

- two without coercion: ZZ32's `=(self, b:IntLiteral)` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:566`) and `=(a:Any, b:Any)` (`:69`);
- 31 with coercion.

The list is in `evidence/inst1-crash-dump.txt`. By `git blame` at `151cb4126`, **24 of the 33 are rung N's** (`a97d60dc6`): `FortressLibrary.fsi:323`, `:325`, `:417-422`, `:566-570`, `:635-639` and `:699-704`. The other 9 (`:69`, `:74`, `:182`, `:322`, `:416`, `:460`, `:565`, `:634` and `:698`) are older. Without N's pairs, 9 candidates are sorted by insertion, which never checks.

### Why this call and not others: the order

The candidates are filtered, in order, from the operator's overloadings. The disambiguator builds that list as `toSet(env.unambiguousFunctionNames(op_name)).map(...) ... .toList` (`scala_src/disambiguator/ExprDisambiguator.scala:870-874`). That is a Scala hash set, iterated in hash order.

- An `Overloading` node's hash covers its unambiguous name (`nodes/Overloading.java:117-130`).
- An `Id` node's hash covers its text (`nodes/Id.java:80-89`).
- That text holds the declaration's file, line and column, for example `_|Library|FortressLibrary.fsi:700:5-31`.

So the order is a function of where the 76 declarations stand. In this run, 65 sorts have 32 or more candidates: 53 of `=` with 33, 8 of `=` with 49, and 4 others with 33 (`evidence/inst1-large-sorts.txt`). Only `:692` throws. `FlatString.fss:105` (`i = -1`) meets the same 33 candidates in another order and passes.

### Which rung's change brought it

- **Not C.** In run inst2, I put C's binding back to the glue class on the merged tree (`FortressBuiltin.fss:665`, `Char$ToExprString`, a one-line edit that moves no line). The crash, the call and the candidate order were all identical to the unchanged tree's (`evidence/inst2-c-reverted-crash.txt`). I did not run C's head on its own. The revert settles it, and by the blame above, C's head has only the 9 older candidates at this call.
- **N brings the input**: 24 of the 33 candidates. On N's own tree the same 24 declarations stand at other lines, and its stage checked `Char` with no crash (`/home/user/fortress-number-open/tmp/rung-number-open/dist-post/run.txt:750`: `FortressBuiltin.fss:624:1-736:2 errors=0`).
- **The trip comes from the composition's lines.** `git log ed8652dc0..151cb4126` shows that F, N, I, A and W changed `FortressLibrary.fsi`, and that F, N, E, I, A, C and W changed `FortressBuiltin.fss`. C's change moves no line.
  - One blank line inserted after `FortressBuiltin.fss:13` (run inst4) moves the 19 local names, and the crash disappears.
  - E's value-object marks and A's change to walk's loader reach the checker only through these line shifts.
  - No single rung other than N is the cause.

### The second row

The second row (`leftover`, "still contains intermediate nodes") follows from the first. Two code facts produce it:

- The shadow keeps the unchecked declaration after a crash (`tools/distance/shadow-patch.py:134-141`).
- `Char`'s unchecked body holds `Juxt` and `MathPrimary` nodes, for example `myJavaDigit(self,10)` and `Just[\ZZ32\](x)`. Both node types are `OutAfterTypeChecking` (`ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast:883`, `:990`).

`assertAfterTypeChecking` then fires. It runs only when the component has no errors (`StaticChecker.java:264`). In runs inst4 and fix1, where `Char` is checked, neither row appears.

## 2. Reproduction and determinism

| run | tree and change (all at `a2f0b5cf2`, path `/home/user/fortress-distcrash`) | extra classes | result | s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| run1 | `distance/run.sh` as tracked | none | both crash rows, `#total 0` (`evidence/run1-table.txt`) | 137 |
| run2 | `shadow-patch.py:142` frames 6 → 400 (printing only) | none | the same rows; the deep stack | 133 |
| inst1 | unchanged | instrumented `Functionals` | `@@SORTX n=33` at `:692`; the 33 candidates and their relation | 138 |
| inst2 | `FortressBuiltin.fss:665` back to `Char$ToExprString` (C undone) | instrumented | the same crash, same candidate order | 152 |
| inst3 | unchanged | instrumented, with pre-candidates | the same crash, same order as inst1 | 138 |
| inst4 | one blank line after `FortressBuiltin.fss:13` | instrumented | no crash; `#total 0`, `#crash none` | 135 |
| fix1 | unchanged library | `:761` as a rank sort | no crash; `#total 0`, `#crash none` | 299 |

Runs inst1 to fix1 run the stage's JVM exactly as `run.sh`'s step 2 does: the same flags, components and shadow classes (run2's), with my classes first on the class path. The script is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/distance-crash/rundist.sh`. `table.py` produced the tables.

**The crash is deterministic for a given tree.** The gate's run on `151cb4126` in `/home/user/fortress`, and run1, run2, inst1 and inst3 on `a2f0b5cf2` in another directory, all crash at `:692`. inst1 and inst3 dump the same candidate order. The order comes from value hashes (class name and name text, with relative paths), not identity hashes, so it does not change from run to run, and the checkout path did not change it. The review's "likely repeat" holds. The gate's "may be intermittent" holds only from edit to edit, not from run to run.

## 3. What the crash hides

- **In `Char`.** The checker checks an object's members in source order (`Decls.scala:164-168`). Before the throw it checked 13 members, from `asString` to `javaDigit`. These include **C's `asExprString`, the second member**, and 12 of `Char`'s 41 bindings. Errors signalled before the throw would have been kept, and the stage printed `typecheck errors=0`. The checker never checked:
  - the rest of `digit(self)` (`:692-693`);
  - `digit(self, radix)` (`:694-713`);
  - the 29 members at `:715-771`, all bindings on `simpleChar`.

  That is 30 members and **29 of the 41 bindings**, in 81 lines (`:692-772`), not 113. The shadow then puts the unchecked `Char` into the component's tree.
- **In `FortressBuiltin`'s later stages:**
  - `leftover` crashed, which is the second row.
  - `wellformed2` and `variance` walked the unchecked `Char`, without its body's types.
  - `overloading` and `export` read declarations' headers through the index, which bodies do not affect.

  Each printed `errors=0`. The count stage is not affected: it checks the `FortressLibrary` component only, and its sorts passed.
- **Measured with the crash avoided** (neither change committed):
  - (a) The blank line after `FortressBuiltin.fss:13` changes no code (inst4). `Char` gives `DECL-OK errors=0`. The table reads `#total 0` and `#crash none` (`evidence/inst4-blank-line.txt`).
  - (b) `Functionals.scala:761` as `val sorted = candidates.sortBy(c => candidates.count(d => !(d eq c) && moreSpecific(d, c)))`, on the unchanged library (fix1). `Char` gives `DECL-OK errors=0`, and the table reads `#total 0` and `#crash none`. But the stage took 299 s against 137 s (`FortressLibrary` 166 s against 86 s), in one run at load about 1 (`evidence/fix1-rank-sort.txt`).

  So **the crash hides 0 errors** on this tree.
- **By reading, not run:** the tracked `StaticChecker` has no per-declaration catch, so after the switch-over a plain `fortress compile` of `FortressBuiltin` with this order would stop on the exception. A user program's `x = -1` over a `ZZ32` meets the same 33 candidates, in its own component's order.

## 4. The ledger row, and the facts made false

**Row**, section "5. Overloading on the compiled path: checker and dispatch". Its text is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/distance-crash/row.txt`. I ran `ledger.py add` against scratch copies of the ledger and its history (`--ledger`/`--history`). It passed the template and would be row 929. The real ledger is unchanged.

    | ? | the compiled checker crashes, 'Comparison method violates its general contract!', at a call with 32 or more applicable candidates: it sorts them by `moreSpecific`, a partial order, with `sortWith`, and Java's TimSort refuses some orders; on climb batch 27's tree, `x = -1` in `Char`'s `digit` | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (checker) | `basic/overloading.tex`, "Overloading Resolution" | explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh | climb batch 27 gate | siblings: `Functionals.scala:728`, `CoercionOracle.scala:255`, `Formula.scala:609`. `Functionals.scala:761`, at a2f0b5cf2: `Ordering.fromLessThan` reads incomparable candidates as equal, which is not transitive; TimSort checks only on 32 or more. `FortressBuiltin.fss:692` meets 33 candidates of `=`, 24 of them rung N's pairs; their order is the hash order of the overloadings' names (`ExprDisambiguator.scala:870-874`), which hold declaration lines, so one blank line at `FortressBuiltin.fss:14` hides it. The distance's two `#crash` rows; the stage keeps `Char` unchecked. Way through: order by rank, at a cost in time. |

**Facts made false:**

- **F-54**: "That gate's `distance.txt` reads `#crash none`" is false: the table has two crash rows. Its next clause, that the checker checks the `FortressLibrary` component to its end without a crash (F-233), stays true.
- **F-281**: "with them checked, the distance and the count are 0, with no crash" is false in "with no crash". So is its gate "the stages ('#total 0', '#crash none'; …)" for the distance.
- **F-288**: "Over the fourteen, the stage reads '#total 0', '#crash none'" is false. Its title, "the compiled checker passes all of them", is false of the gate's run, because the checker crashed in `FortressBuiltin`. It is true once `Char` is checked: inst4 and fix1 read 0.
- **F-53**: its figures, 0 and 0, stand. Its "nothing crashes (F-233)" describes the count, which still reads `#crash none`. Run inst4 shows that its distance zero also holds with `Char` checked whole. That "last landed" waits on the push is the review's point; my runs bear on neither.

## 5. Against the review's reading (`explorations/reviews/batch-27-review.md`, section 7, point 6; split 10; finding A)

- "the cause is C's binding, or C's binding with another rung's lines": **refuted.** The crash stays with C's binding undone (inst2). The trigger is N's 24 `=` pairs, in the composed tree's line positions.
- "C's moved binding … has so far no completed check against its helper": **refuted.** It is `Char`'s second member, checked with no error before the throw in the gate's own run, and checked again in inst4 and fix1.
- "an error in its 113 lines past the throw is not counted": the throw is at `:692`, and 81 lines follow it, with 30 members and 29 bindings unchecked. Measured with the crash avoided, they hold 0 errors.
- "Which sort raised it, I could not tell": it is `Functionals.scala:761`.
- Confirmed: some call in `Char`'s body met 32 or more candidates (`x = -1`, 33). The second row follows from the first. The crash repeats on the same tree.

## 6. Disk and cleanup

Before the work, `df` showed 4.8G free; the worktree took 245M at its largest. I removed it with `git worktree remove --force /home/user/fortress-distcrash` and `git worktree prune`. It was detached, so there is no branch. Afterwards `df` showed 4.8G free. The scratchpad holds this report, `row.txt`, `rundist.sh`, `evidence/` (84K) and `dry/` (copies of the ledger used for the row check).

Over the 33 candidates the relation holds 231 pairs. It is irreflexive, never holds both ways, and is transitive, so it is a strict partial order. But incomparability is not transitive, in 3,880 triples. One of them:

- `(BigNum, ZZ64) ≺ (BigNum, ZZ)`;
- `(QQ, NN32)` is incomparable with both.

TimSort checks only when it sorts 32 or more items; below that it sorts by insertion and checks nothing. Three other sorts use a partial order the same way: `Functionals.scala:728`, `CoercionOracle.scala:255`, and `Formula.scala:609`. The last is worse: its `subtype(b,a)` is reflexive, so it compares an item with itself as less.
